sections.h2: What are my options if I need to sell in Halfmoon quickly?
sections.html:
A Halfmoon owner who needs speed has an agent listing, a sale handled alone, and a direct purchase by a cash buyer who accepts the house in its current condition. Only the third removes showings and repair work from the schedule. A listing in good condition may reach a higher price, but it asks for months of patience.

Halfmoon sits in the southeast corner of Saratoga County, between the Hudson and Mohawk Rivers, and the questions sellers raise here are practical ones: what the assessor has on file, which permits exist, and where the deed goes. This page answers those in order.

  • Agent listing: suits a tidy house and an owner who can host showings through an appraisal.
  • Selling alone: saves the commission but leaves pricing, contracts and transfer forms on you.
  • Cash purchase: fits an estate property, deferred repairs, a tenant-occupied rental, or a tax or mortgage deadline.

sections.h2: What housing figures does the Census publish for Halfmoon?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists Halfmoon at 26,658 people for mid-2025, a rise of 3.9% on the 2020 estimates base. Two-thirds of homes (67.2%) are owner-occupied, and owner-occupied units carry a median value of $387,700 for the 2020 to 2024 survey years.

Renters pay a median $1,559 a month. Household income has a median of $100,712 in 2024 dollars across 11,525 households of about 2.27 people each, and the average commute is 23.7 minutes. Those figures describe a mostly owner-occupied suburb, so compare any cash number against recent Halfmoon sales before you answer it.

With 32.58 square miles of land, the town had roughly 788 residents per square mile at the 2020 count. That mix of subdivisions and open land explains why lot size and road frontage vary so widely from one Halfmoon street to the next.

sections.h2: How is Halfmoon laid out, and why does that matter to a buyer?
sections.html:
Halfmoon is a town of hamlets rather than a single downtown, and where your house sits decides who is likely to buy it. Its population has climbed in every census since 1960, reaching 25,662 in 2020.

The southern line follows the Mohawk River and the eastern line follows the Hudson. The Anthony Kill marks the north, and McDonald Creek runs through the middle. The Adirondack Northway (I-87) runs along the western edge, US 9 crosses in over the Crescent Bridge, US 4 serves the east, and NY 146 and NY 236 meet near Newtown. Commuters heading for Albany ask about drive time before anything else.

  • Crescent: a southern hamlet where US 9 crosses the Mohawk.
  • Halfmoon hamlet: the junction of County Roads 94, 95, 96 and 99.
  • Newtown: the northeastern hamlet at the junction of NY 236, NY 146 and County Road 86.
  • Coons and Halfmoon Beach: a northern hamlet and a riverside hamlet in the southwest, the latter now largely covered by a residential development.

The Erie Canal and the Champlain Canal both ran through the town in the 1800s, and the town filled about 1.5 miles of the Erie Canal in 1962. If your lot sits near a former canal route or a river bank, expect a buyer to ask about drainage and flood history.

sections.h2: Which school districts tax Halfmoon parcels?
sections.html:
Three districts levy school tax on Halfmoon parcels: Shenendehowa, Mechanicville and Waterford-Halfmoon. The Halfmoon Assessment Office lists them as taxing jurisdictions alongside Saratoga County and various special districts.

The district named on your bill shapes what a buyer pays each year, so read that line before you set an asking price. Neighbors on opposite sides of a district boundary can pay quite different school tax. The town says school bills are issued in September and county bills follow in January.

sections.h2: How does Halfmoon assess a property, and which dates matter?
sections.html:
Each year the Assessment Office updates values and files the roll that the county, the three school districts and special districts rely on. The last town-wide revaluation was finished in 1996, so assessed values in Halfmoon reflect a long gap since the last full reappraisal.

The office values a property as it stood on March 1, the taxable status date. Work finished after that date waits for the next cycle, and exemption applications have to reach the office by the same day. The STAR credit does not show on the roll because it is a credit, not an exemption.

Halfmoon assessment calendar (source: Town of Halfmoon Assessment Office)
DateWhat happens
March 1Taxable status date; exemption applications due
May 1Tentative assessment roll filed; grievance forms accepted from this day
4th Tuesday of MayGrievance Day before the five-member Board of Assessment Review
July 1Final roll filed with Board of Assessment Review changes
September and JanuarySchool tax bills, then county tax bills

Only the assessment can be contested, never the bill, and a late filing is dismissed. A seller closing in spring should tell the buyer where the property stands on this calendar.

sections.h2: What paperwork should Halfmoon sellers gather first?
sections.html:
Begin with the town's Building and Code Enforcement office. It applies the state fire and building codes plus local laws, reviews construction drawings, and tells owners to call before starting work if they are unsure a permit is needed.

A Halfmoon building permit file typically holds a plot plan with distances to the property line, well and septic placement where relevant, three sets of plans, and contractor insurance forms. Driveways may need a curb cut permit from the Highway Department, NYS DOT or Saratoga County DPW, and some lots need a county sewer permit. A buyer's attorney will want the paper trail for any addition, garage or finished basement.

  • Locate plot plans and permits for each addition or outbuilding.
  • Read your bill for the school and special districts that levy on the parcel.
  • Ask the Assessment Office which exemptions end when title passes.
  • Confirm whether the house is on septic or sewer.

sections.h2: Where is a Halfmoon deed recorded, and what tax comes with it?
sections.html:
Saratoga County Clerk handles it, at 40 McMaster Street in Ballston Spa, taking land recordings until 4:15 in the afternoon. That office files over 85,000 documents a year, among them deeds, mortgages and discharges.

The state levies $2 for every $500 of price, rounded up, on the transfer. A house that sells for $387,700, the Census median for Halfmoon, therefore carries $1,552. The seller is the usual payer, with Form TP-584 filed alongside the deed no later than the 15th day after delivery. Buyers of residences at $1 million or more owe a further 1%.

Because school and county bills arrive months apart, closing figures usually split each one by days of ownership. Ask the Assessment Office what exemptions are on file so the numbers on the closing statement hold no surprises.

faqs.q: Is a cash purchase in Halfmoon really quicker than a listing?
faqs.a: Usually, because no lender or appraisal sits between the offer and the deed. What remains is title work and filing at the Saratoga County Clerk. Get a written closing date from any buyer before agreeing.

faqs.q: Must the roof or kitchen be repaired before a Halfmoon sale?
faqs.a: No repair is required by law for a sale. Buyers who pay cash take the property in its present state. Your real exposure is unpermitted work, so assemble permits for additions from the Building and Code Enforcement office.

faqs.q: What does the seller owe the state at a Halfmoon closing?
faqs.a: New York transfer tax of $2 per $500, with the buyer liable only if the seller fails to pay or is exempt. The extra 1% on residences of $1 million or more falls on the buyer.

faqs.q: Can a Halfmoon owner dispute an assessment ahead of a sale?
faqs.a: Yes, through a complaint on the tentative roll between May 1 and Grievance Day, the fourth Tuesday of May. The five-member Board of Assessment Review rules on the evidence. Tax bills cannot be grieved.

faqs.q: Whose school tax will a Halfmoon buyer pay?
faqs.a: That of Shenendehowa, Mechanicville or Waterford-Halfmoon, depending on where the parcel lies. The September bill is usually prorated on the closing statement.
